lead: Test of 0.8.44 with the CI test build 45879876669 of the round head (7747749): the fixes from the research run (original vs ours, T1-T23: bank sync that goes on past a dead slot, bank check at every connect, broker writes and Windows reads, Control Center refused while a plug-in plays, backups read fresh, 4 ms audio pieces, original projects with routing) and the clean bank sync (no notes and no clock while it runs, like the original). Already done on the local build: hil.sh H1-H6, a block sweep 32-512 at 44.1/48 kHz, a full 512-patch sync with notes (silent, cache identical), your REAPER smoke test and Virus off/on (E603). risk.py: class C on all three systems; by hand: Virus off/on everywhere, sleep on the Mac. Mark each item and add a note where something looks different; Claude reads the marks from this page.
rules: Order: Linux first (the Virus is there), then the Windows VM, later the Mac. Close the DAW before the Virus moves.
Never power-cycle the Virus while it is attached to the VM without telling Claude first (Claude re-attaches it afterwards).
Use a disposable project. Only L5 and L6 write to the Virus, and only into the RAM bank you name in the note (the plug-in and the Control Center back it up first).
No game or other heavy program running during the timing items.

sections.title: Linux
sections.where: This PC, REAPER, the 0.8.44 CI build (installed by Claude)
prep: Nothing to install. Claude installs the CI build, runs hil.sh and posts the result here.

items.title: Automated core run (Claude runs it)
steps: Claude runs scripts/hil.sh --sleep with the installed CI build (asks for your password once), then the block sweep 32-512 at both rates.
items.expect: ALL PASS: cold start, two reopens, export, broker killed while playing, sleep; the sweep without drops.

items.title: Clean bank sync at the start
steps: Open a project with a MIDI clip on the TI Revive track and press Play right away, while the plug-in shows its start-up page.
Keep playing until the editor appears.
items.expect: Nothing plays during the start-up and the short bank check (about 12 s in all with a full cache), then every note plays on time. No "SYNC PAUSED" text, no hanging note.

items.title: Virus switched on after the DAW, and a replug while playing
steps: Switch the Virus off, open the project, then switch the Virus on.
Play, then pull the USB cable for 5 s and plug it in again while it plays.
items.expect: Both times the plug-in finds the Virus by itself, runs its bank check and plays on within about 20 s; no note hangs after the replug.

items.title: Loading a project while notes play
steps: Play a clip with long notes, then open a second project with a different patch (or undo a patch change in REAPER) while it plays.
items.expect: What sounded stops, the new patch is there and the next notes play with it; nothing hangs.

items.title: SAVE with Compare, sort, and closing during a sort
steps: Name a RAM bank you can lose (note it here). Edit a patch, press Compare, then SAVE it into a slot of that bank.
Sort that bank by name, and close REAPER right after starting the sort. Open the project again.
items.expect: The stored patch is the edited one, not the one Compare showed. The sort is complete after reopening (closing waits up to 20 s for it). A backup of the overwritten slots is in the backup folder.

items.title: Control Center: refused while playing, then backup and restore
steps: With REAPER playing, open the Control Center and its RAM bank list.
Close REAPER. Back up the bank from L5, then restore it into the same bank.
items.expect: While the plug-in plays, the bank list, backup and restore say the Virus is in use. Without it, the backup is made, the restore saves "RAM X before restore ..." first and the bank matches the backup.

items.title: An original Access project with part routing
steps: Open a project saved with the original plug-in whose parts go to other outputs (USB 2/3) or use detune.
items.expect: The parts come out on the same outputs as with the original, with their detune.

sections.title: Windows 11 VM
sections.where: win11 VM, Ableton Live, the 0.8.44 CI build (installed by Claude, setup.exe /quiet)
prep: Claude passes the Virus through to the VM and runs hil-win for the automated core items.

items.title: Automated core run (Claude runs it)
steps: Claude runs hil-win in the VM with the installed CI build.
items.expect: ALL PASS (cold start, two reopens, export, broker killed while playing).

items.title: Plays in Live over ASIO at small and large buffers
steps: Play a busy clip for a minute each at ASIO buffers 64, 256 and 1024 (TI Revive Audio).
items.expect: No crackles or drop-outs at any buffer; Live's latency shown changes with the buffer.

items.title: Control Center while Live plays
steps: With Live playing, open the Control Center and try its RAM bank list and a backup. Then close Live and try again.
items.expect: Refused with a clear message while Live plays; works after Live is closed.

items.title: Clean bank sync and project load in Live
steps: Open the project and play right away (as L2), then load another project while it plays (as L4).

sections.title: macOS
sections.where: MacBook Air M3, Ableton Live 12 and Logic, the 0.8.44 CI build 45879876669
prep: Plug the Mac into power. Move the Virus' USB cable to the Mac.
Quit every DAW, then double-click Install test build.command in the folder Claude names in the chat (asks for your password). Claude checks the installed files afterwards.

items.title: Automated core run (you start it, Claude grades it)
steps: Double-click hil-mac.command in the test build folder and wait for it to finish (about 5 minutes).
items.expect: ALL PASS (Claude grades the results folder).

items.title: Clean bank sync, project load and playing in Live and Logic
steps: In Live: L2 and L4. In Logic: open a project with the Audio Unit and play for a minute.
items.expect: Same as L2 and L4; Logic plays without drop-outs.
